# Researching and ingesting wiki evidence

Choose the mode explicitly from the request. An unspecified request to use this
role is not permission to process the whole backlog; clarify the intended task.
Treat `` as the request when the host has not substituted it.

- **Discover sources on a topic:** read [discovery](references/discover.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md),
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md), and
  [efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md). Research perspectives
  return candidates without writing. Use the capture route only within the
  requested scope; a request for candidates alone remains read-only.
- **Capture named URLs or saved web pages:** read [named capture](references/capture.md)
  and [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md). Skip broad topic research;
  preserve deduplication, declines and capture checks.
- **Capture a named format or service:** read its complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or
  [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md). These routes include prerequisite
  checks; missing converters or authentication never justify fabricated evidence.
- **Ingest named existing clippings:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), and
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md). Use the exact source set;
  do not rediscover it or silently expand to the global backlog.
- **Process new or un-ingested clippings without a filename:** read
  [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join backlog contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Determine eligibility before writing. Preserve already summarized sources and
  reject restricted evidence as support. If nothing eligible is pending, report
  that without opening an operation, logging, committing or refreshing indexes.

Capture-only requests create evidence, never derived source or concept pages.
Ingestion needs authorization for that source set; an explicitly requested full
research-and-ingest flow already provides it. Only capture tools write raw
artifacts, and agents never edit their bodies. Read
[evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before assessing fidelity,
quoting or synthesizing; preserve restrictions and platform-specific sections.

Before the first authorized mutation, read
[operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md). Finish the
scoped validation, log, commit, sync and remote verification unless publication
is held. Reuse an enclosing operation when it owns the work; preserve other
writers' edits. For concept reuse and relationship changes read
[efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).
Mode: capture a named Word format. I need the complete Word route, so I'll read it now.

5	# Clipping a Word document into the wiki
6	
7	The HTML clipper (`clip.mjs` → Defuddle) handles **HTML** pages only, and
8	`clip-pdf` handles **PDFs**. A `.docx`/`.doc` — e.g. an Academia.edu paper served
9	as Word rather than PDF — falls to neither, and clicking its "Download" is often
10	the *only* way to get the source. This reference covers the Word path. **The canonical
11	stored artifact is the extracted Markdown, never the binary document** — that keeps
12	the vault greppable, diffable, and answerable, and makes `[[note]]` provenance
13	resolve to a real Markdown clipping rather than to an opaque attachment.
14	
15	## How it works
16	
17	`clip-docx.mjs` extracts text with **pandoc** (invoked via Node's `execFileSync`,
18	which resolves the Windows `.exe` correctly — do **not** shell out to `pandoc` from
19	a Bash tool per the PATHEXT hazard), then writes `raw/clippings/<slug>.md` with the
20	standard clipping frontmatter (`source`, `created`, `tags:[clippings]`, `quality`,
21	`source-hash`). It skips duplicates and prior declines, and records a decline for a
22	**thin** extraction (empty or near-empty document) so it is not retried blindly.
23	Pass **`--allow-short`** to clip a document that is genuinely brief — see step 2.
24	
25	It deliberately mirrors `clip-pdf` but **omits the PDF-only machinery**:
26	- **No running header/footer stripping.** A `.docx` has no fixed pages, so pandoc
27	  emits no page-boundary chrome to strip (unlike `pdftotext`'s form-feeds).
28	- **No `fidelity: degraded` / OCR.** pandoc reads the document's XML directly, so
29	  there is no symbol-font mangling to flag and no scanned-image case to OCR — the
30	  extraction is clean Unicode prose. (A genuinely corrupt or password-protected
31	  file fails fast and is reported for manual handling, not invented.)
32	- **`--wrap=none`.** Prevents pandoc from hard-wrapping paragraphs at 72 columns,
33	  which would break verbatim spans across synthetic line breaks; `-t plain` strips
34	  markup to quotable prose in reading order.
35	
36	## Steps
37	
38	1. **Preflight** (once): confirm pandoc is installed — `pandoc -v`. If missing,
39	   tell the user to install pandoc (https://pandoc.org/installing.html) and stop;
40	   do not fabricate content.
41	2. **Clip** (this is the only writer to `raw/` for Word docs):
42	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-docx.mjs" "<path/to/file.docx>" --source="<canonical-url-if-any>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>"`
43	   - `--source` is the citable origin (the paper's DOI/URL). Omit for a purely
44	     local file and the file path is recorded as the source.
45	   - **`--topic` whenever this clip belongs to a research run** — pass the topic
46	     string researcher discovery was given, identical across every clip in the run,
47	     so maintainer triage can group the run's leftovers together. **Topic is recorded
48	     going forward only and no tool can retro-fit it**, so a clip made without it
49	     is an *Unattributed* triage row permanently. Omit it only when there is no
50	     research run behind the clip; never invent one.
51	   - A `thin` or `failed` result means the document is empty/corrupt/protected —
52	     report it for manual handling; do not invent the text.
53	   - **`--allow-short` when the document is short on purpose.** The thin floor is
54	     100 words, and word count cannot tell a failed extraction apart from a
55	     complete one-page handout — a bare list, a blank worksheet, a vocabulary
56	     sheet. Open the file, confirm the extraction is whole, then re-clip with the
57	     flag. It is opt-in per clip precisely so every other clip keeps the safety

63	4. **Only when ingestion is authorized, follow [ingestion](ingest.md)** for this exact clipping — summarize

70	- `clip-docx.mjs` is the **sole writer** to `raw/` for Word documents — the model
71	  never writes the clipping by hand (that would bypass dedup, decline, and hashing).
72	- **Fidelity, not truth**: a faithful extraction of a wrong paper is still wrong;
73	  pandoc can also drop table/figure structure — verify quotes against the document
74	  before they land on a wiki page (guardrail #5).

# Clipping a Word document into the wiki

The HTML clipper (`clip.mjs` → Defuddle) handles **HTML** pages only, and
`clip-pdf` handles **PDFs**. A `.docx`/`.doc` — e.g. an Academia.edu paper served
as Word rather than PDF — falls to neither, and clicking its "Download" is often
the *only* way to get the source. This reference covers the Word path. **The canonical
stored artifact is the extracted Markdown, never the binary document** — that keeps
the vault greppable, diffable, and answerable, and makes `[[note]]` provenance
resolve to a real Markdown clipping rather than to an opaque attachment.

## How it works

`clip-docx.mjs` extracts text with **pandoc** (invoked via Node's `execFileSync`,
which resolves the Windows `.exe` correctly — do **not** shell out to `pandoc` from
a Bash tool per the PATHEXT hazard), then writes `raw/clippings/<slug>.md` with the
standard clipping frontmatter (`source`, `created`, `tags:[clippings]`, `quality`,
`source-hash`). It skips duplicates and prior declines, and records a decline for a
**thin** extraction (empty or near-empty document) so it is not retried blindly.
Pass **`--allow-short`** to clip a document that is genuinely brief — see step 2.

It deliberately mirrors `clip-pdf` but **omits the PDF-only machinery**:
- **No running header/footer stripping.** A `.docx` has no fixed pages, so pandoc
  emits no page-boundary chrome to strip (unlike `pdftotext`'s form-feeds).
- **No `fidelity: degraded` / OCR.** pandoc reads the document's XML directly, so
  there is no symbol-font mangling to flag and no scanned-image case to OCR — the
  extraction is clean Unicode prose. (A genuinely corrupt or password-protected
  file fails fast and is reported for manual handling, not invented.)
- **`--wrap=none`.** Prevents pandoc from hard-wrapping paragraphs at 72 columns,
  which would break verbatim spans across synthetic line breaks; `-t plain` strips
  markup to quotable prose in reading order.

## Steps

1. **Preflight** (once): confirm pandoc is installed — `pandoc -v`. If missing,
   tell the user to install pandoc (https://pandoc.org/installing.html) and stop;
   do not fabricate content.
2. **Clip** (this is the only writer to `raw/` for Word docs):
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-docx.mjs" "<path/to/file.docx>" --source="<canonical-url-if-any>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>"`
   - `--source` is the citable origin (the paper's DOI/URL). Omit for a purely
     local file and the file path is recorded as the source.
   - **`--topic` whenever this clip belongs to a research run** — pass the topic
     string researcher discovery was given, identical across every clip in the run,
     so maintainer triage can group the run's leftovers together. **Topic is recorded
     going forward only and no tool can retro-fit it**, so a clip made without it
     is an *Unattributed* triage row permanently. Omit it only when there is no
     research run behind the clip; never invent one.
   - A `thin` or `failed` result means the document is empty/corrupt/protected —
     report it for manual handling; do not invent the text.
   - **`--allow-short` when the document is short on purpose.** The thin floor is
     100 words, and word count cannot tell a failed extraction apart from a
     complete one-page handout — a bare list, a blank worksheet, a vocabulary
     sheet. Open the file, confirm the extraction is whole, then re-clip with the
     flag. It is opt-in per clip precisely so every other clip keeps the safety
     net: never reach for it to push past a document you have not looked at, and
     never use it on one whose text pandoc actually failed to read.
3. **Verify** the clipping landed: read `raw/clippings/<slug>.md` and sanity-check
   that the extracted text is real prose. pandoc output is plain text — light and
   lossy on tables/figures.
4. **Only when ingestion is authorized, follow [ingestion](ingest.md)** for this exact clipping — summarize
   into `wiki/sources/`, cross-reference, index, log. Ingestion requires authorization for this scope; reuse explicit session authorization.

## Guardrails

- **Never edit the body of anything under `raw/`** — clipped text is immutable
  source-of-truth (guardrail #1). Frontmatter is pipeline state, tooling-only.
- `clip-docx.mjs` is the **sole writer** to `raw/` for Word documents — the model
  never writes the clipping by hand (that would bypass dedup, decline, and hashing).
- **Fidelity, not truth**: a faithful extraction of a wrong paper is still wrong;
  pandoc can also drop table/figure structure — verify quotes against the document
  before they land on a wiki page (guardrail #5).

## Completion

For a standalone clip, open an operation before the clipping helper writes, verify
its returned paths and extraction diagnostics, log once, commit, push and verify
remote publication through the shared operations contract. During discovery,
use the enclosing operation and report the results to its owner for completion.
Pass `--since <saved-token>` to the clipping helper so every written path enters
that operation's ledger. Capture-only requests end after this completion and
create no derived source or concept pages.
Capturing evidence does not by itself authorize ingestion; reuse explicit
discover-and-ingest authorization when it is already present.
